canonicalFacts.claim: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer mortality worldwide
About 90% of lung cancer cases are caused by smoking and tobacco use
Lung cancer is divided into small-cell lung carcinomas (SCLCs) and non-small cell lung carcinomas (NSCLCs)
Targeted therapies and immunotherapies have radically improved treatment for advanced NSCLC
Actionable genomic alterations are mostly found in lung adenocarcinomas
Low-dose computed tomography screening can reduce lung cancer mortality

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Avoid smoking and tobacco products as they cause about 90% of lung cancer cases
Minimize exposure to radon gas, asbestos, and air pollution which can contribute to lung carcinogenesis

redFlags: Lung cancer often presents at advanced stages with poor prognosis
Drug resistance frequently develops with targeted therapies
Multiple inherited and acquired susceptibility mechanisms exist
